extracted.intended_audience: Community and non-community public water system operators, and State drinking water program authorities responsible for monitoring, assessment, reporting, and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and criteria for total coliform and E. coli monitoring, triggers, assessments, corrective actions, reporting/recordkeeping, and related PFAS analytical and reporting deadlines for public water systems under 40 CFR part 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for returning to quarterly monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce monitoring frequency for a system on monthly monitoring to quarterly if the system meets the criteria in paragraphs (g)(1) and (g)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (g)(1) Within the last 12 months the system must have a completed sanitary survey or site visit by the State or a voluntary Level 2 assessment by a party approved by the State, be free of sanitary defects, and have a protected water source; and (g)(2) the system must have a clean compliance history for a minimum of 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for systems on increased monitoring to qualify for annual monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce monitoring for a system on increased monitoring to annual if it meets paragraph (g) criteria plus paragraphs (h)(1) and (h)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (h)(1) An annual State site visit and correction of all identified sanitary defects (or substitute voluntary Level 2 assessment by a State-approved party). (h)(2) The system must have in place or adopt one or more additional enhancements to water system barriers listed in (h)(2)(i)-(v): cross connection control approved by State; certified operator or regular certified circuit rider visits; continuous disinfection with residual per State criteria; demonstration of maintenance of at least 4-log virus removal/inactivation per §141.403(b)(3); or other equivalent enhancements approved by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal systems start-up and monitoring frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning April 1, 2016, seasonal systems must demonstrate completion of a State-approved start-up procedure and normally must monitor every month they are in operation unless they meet criteria for less frequent monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start-up procedure may include start-up sampling prior to serving water. To monitor less frequently than monthly, seasonal systems must have an approved sample siting plan designating the monitoring period (e.g., highest demand/vulnerability) and collect compliance samples during that period. Eligibility for quarterly or annual monitoring requires meeting the criteria in paragraphs (g) or (h), respectively. The State may exempt seasonal systems if the distribution system remains pressurized during the non-operating period, but systems monitoring less frequently than monthly must still monitor during the State-designated vulnerable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional routine monitoring following a total coliform-positive sample (quarterly/annual systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems on quarterly or annual frequency must conduct additional routine monitoring the month following one or more total coliform-positive samples and must collect at least three routine samples during the next month, unless the State waives this requirement under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may collect additional samples spread across the month or all on one day from different sites. Results are used in coliform treatment technique trigger calculations. State may waive the three-sample requirement if: (1) State or approved agent performs a sufficiently detailed site visit before month end (not performed by system employee); (2) State determines cause and documents in writing that problem corrected or will be corrected before month's end, with supervisor approval and availability to EPA/public; or (3) State cannot waive solely because all repeat samples are TC-negative, except where State determines problem corrected before repeat samples and all repeats were TC-negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine monitoring frequency for community water systems using only ground water (<=1,000 people)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ground-water-only community systems serving 1,000 or fewer people, monitoring frequency for total coliforms is one sample per month, subject to transition and reduction provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following any TC-positive sample systems must comply with repeat monitoring and E. coli requirements (§141.858). After completing monthly monitoring and repeat/E. coli requirements, systems must determine whether any coliform treatment technique triggers (§141.859) have been exceeded and complete assessments if so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to subpart Y special monitoring evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning April 1, 2016, States must perform a special monitoring evaluation during each sanitary survey to review system status and determine appropriate monitoring schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After evaluation, State may modify monitoring schedule only if system has met applicable criteria; State may not allow less frequent monitoring under special evaluation unless system already meets criteria in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for reduced monitoring (ground-water systems <=1,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: State may reduce monitoring from monthly to no less than quarterly if system complies with State-certified operator provisions and meets criteria in (d)(1)(i)-(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Clean compliance history for at least 12 months; (ii) Most recent sanitary survey shows system free of sanitary defects (or has approved plan/schedule to correct and is in compliance), has protected source and meets approved construction standards; (iii) System meets at least one of: annual site visit equivalent to Level 2 or annual Level 2 assessment by State-approved party with correction of defects; cross connection control approved by State; continuous disinfection with residual per State criteria; demonstration of ≥4-log virus removal/inactivation per §141.403(b)(3); or other equivalent State-approved enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events triggering return to monthly monitoring (ground-water systems <=1,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems on quarterly monitoring must begin monthly monitoring the month following certain events and continue until they meet reduced monitoring requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers: (1) system triggers a Level 2 assessment or two Level 1 assessments in a rolling 12-month period; (2) system has an E. coli MCL violation; (3) system has a coliform treatment technique violation; (4) system has two subpart Y monitoring violations in a rolling 12-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine monitoring frequency for subpart H systems (<=1,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H systems (including consecutive systems) serving 1,000 or fewer must monitor monthly and may not reduce monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seasonal system provisions apply (State-approved start-up procedure; possible State exemption if distribution remains pressurized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfiltered subpart H turbidity-triggered coliform sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: An unfiltered subpart H system that does not practice filtration in compliance must collect at least one TC sample near the first service connection each day source water turbidity exceeds 1 NTU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample must be collected within 24 hours of first exceedance unless State determines logistical inability to analyze within 30 hours and identifies alternative schedule. These coliform sample results count toward coliform treatment technique trigger determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency for public water systems serving >1,000 people
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring frequency for total coliforms is based on population served with a specified table of minimum number of samples per month (ranges from 2 to 480 depending on population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must follow the numeric table mapping population brackets to minimum monthly samples. After completing monitoring and repeats/E. coli requirements, systems must determine if any coliform treatment technique triggers (§141.859) are exceeded and complete assessments if so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring exceptions for systems serving fluctuating populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may not reduce monitoring except for non-community ground-water-only systems serving ≤1,000 in some months and >1,000 in others; in months >1,000 they must monitor at frequencies specified for >1,000, and in months ≤1,000 State may reduce frequency in writing consistent with §141.854 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must take into account provisions in §141.854(e)-(g) when reducing monitoring frequency in months serving ≤1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat monitoring timing and quantity following a TC-positive sample
rubrics_metrics.description: If a routine sample is total coliform-positive, system must collect a set of repeat samples within 24 hours of being notified and must collect no fewer than three repeat samples for each TC-positive sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may extend 24-hour limit case-by-case for logistical problems and must specify extension period; State cannot waive requirement to collect repeat samples. All repeat samples should be collected on the same day except State may allow single-connection systems to collect over three days or collect larger volume samples totaling at least 300 ml. Additional sets required if any repeat sample is TC-positive and must be collected within 24 hours of notification (unless State extends). Systems must continue until one complete set is TC-not-detected or system determines a coliform treatment technique trigger (§141.859(a)) has been exceeded and notifies State. If trigger is exceeded due to a routine sample, only one round of repeat monitoring is required for that routine sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting subsequent routine samples as repeat samples when collected nearby
rubrics_metrics.description: If system collects another routine sample(s) from within five adjacent service connections of an initial routine sample before learning the initial sample's result, and the initial sample is later found TC-positive, the subsequent sample(s) may be counted as repeat samples instead of routine samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of all routine and repeat samples not invalidated by the State must be used to determine whether a coliform treatment technique trigger (§141.859) has been exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli testing and notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine or repeat sample is TC-positive, the system must analyze that TC-positive culture medium to determine if E. coli are present and must notify the State by the end of the day when the system is notified of the result (with limited exception for after-hours notification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notified after State office is closed and State lacks after-hours procedures, system must notify State before end of next business day. State may allow a system to forgo E. coli testing on a case-by-case basis if system assumes TC-positive sample is E. coli-positive; in that case, system must notify State as required and §141.63(c) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coliform treatment technique triggers (Level 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct assessments after exceeding treatment technique triggers: Level 1 triggers include, for systems taking ≥40 samples/month exceeding 5.0% TC-positive samples for the month; for systems taking <40 samples/month, having two or more TC-positive samples in the same month; or failing to take every required repeat sample after any single TC-positive sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Level 1 trigger exceeded, system must conduct Level 1 assessment consistent with State requirements as soon as practical and submit completed Level 1 assessment form to State within 30 days after learning of trigger. Assessment form must describe sanitary defects detected, corrective actions completed, and timetable for corrective actions not completed (or note no defects). State reviews and may request revisions within an agreed schedule not exceeding 30 days from consultation; upon review State determines if likely cause identified and corrected or has acceptable schedule for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coliform treatment technique triggers (Level 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Level 2 triggers include an E. coli MCL violation; a second Level 1 trigger within a rolling 12-month period unless State has determined likely reason for first trigger and established correction; or, for systems with approved annual monitoring, a Level 1 trigger in two consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Level 2 trigger exceeded the system must ensure a Level 2 assessment is conducted by the State or a party approved by the State as soon as practical and submit a completed Level 2 assessment form to the State within 30 days after learning of the trigger. Level 2 assessment form must describe sanitary defects detected, corrective actions completed, and a timetable for remaining corrections. System may conduct Level 2 assessments if staff/management have State-specified certification/qualifications unless State directs otherwise. State may require expedited or additional actions in case of an E. coli MCL violation. State reviews and may require revisions as with Level 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment minimum elements and tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors must evaluate minimum elements including sample site adequacy, sampling protocol, sample processing, atypical events affecting distributed water quality, changes in distribution system maintenance/operation, source/treatment considerations, and existing water quality monitoring data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments must be consistent with any State directives tailoring specific elements with respect to size/type of system and distribution system characteristics. Level 2 assessments must be conducted by parties approved by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action and timetable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must correct sanitary defects found through Level 1 or Level 2 assessments and complete corrective actions in compliance with a timetable approved by the State if not completed by submission time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System must notify the State when each scheduled corrective action is completed. Failure to conduct required assessments or corrective actions within required timeframes constitutes a treatment technique violation (§141.860(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation between system and State
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time during assessment or corrective action phases, either the water system or the State may request consultation with the other to determine appropriate actions, methods, timeframes, and other relevant information impacting ability to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation may address method of accomplishment, appropriate timeframes, and other factors relevant to compliance with this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli MCL violation definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A system is in violation of the MCL for E. coli when any of the specified conditions occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violating conditions include: (1) an E. coli-positive repeat sample following a TC-positive routine sample; (2) a TC-positive repeat sample following an E. coli-positive routine sample; (3) failure to take all required repeat samples following an E. coli-positive routine sample; (4) failure to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests TC-positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring violations definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring violations include failure to take every required routine or additional routine sample in a compliance period and failure to analyze for E. coli following a TC-positive routine sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such failures are expressly categorized as monitoring violations under §141.860(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting violations definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting violations include failure to submit a monitoring report or completed assessment form after properly conducting monitoring or assessment in a timely manner; failure to notify the State following an E. coli-positive sample in a timely manner; and failure to submit certification of completion of State-approved start-up procedure by a seasonal system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific timelines for notifications and report submissions are given in §141.861 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli and treatment technique notification timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must notify the State by the end of the day when they learn of an E. coli MCL violation or when notified of an E. coli-positive routine sample, unless result learned after State office closed and State lacks after-hours procedures, in which case notification must be before end of next business day. Systems with treatment technique violations must report to State no later than the end of the next business day and notify the public in accordance with subpart Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment reports must be submitted within 30 days; systems that fail to comply with monitoring must report monitoring violations to the State within 10 days after discovery; seasonal systems must certify completion of State-approved start-up prior to serving public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for assessments and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must maintain any assessment form and documentation of corrective actions or summaries of sanitary defects and corrective actions for State review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must be kept for not less than five years after completion of the assessment or corrective action. Systems must also maintain records of any repeat sample that meets State criteria for extension of the 24-hour collection period.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS subpart applicability and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart Z constitutes national primary drinking water regulations for PFAS; each community water system (CWS) and non-transient non-community water system (NTNCWS) must meet subpart requirements including MCLs identified in §141.61(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: meet analytical requirements in §141.901 by June 25, 2024; report initial monitoring results to State by April 26, 2027; meet compliance monitoring requirements by April 26, 2027; meet MCL compliance requirements by April 26, 2029; meet reporting and recordkeeping requirements by April 26, 2027. Violations (monitoring/reporting/MCL) may be assessed starting on specified dates (monitoring/reporting: beginning April 26, 2027; MCL: beginning April 26, 2029).

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS analytical method restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use only the analytical methods specified in §141.901 to demonstrate compliance with the PFAS subpart requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section incorporates by reference EPA Method 533 and Method 537.1 (version 2.0) and provides information on where the documents can be inspected/obtained (EPA, NARA, EPA PFAS laboratory methods webpage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods for specific PFAS contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulated PFAS must be measured using the listed methods in Table 1 to paragraph (b)(1), mapping specific contaminants to EPA methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists contaminants (PFBS, PFHxS, PFNA, PFOS, PFOA, HFPO-DA/GenX) with methodology SPE LC-MS/MS and EPA methods 533 and 537.1 version 2.0 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification for PFAS analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses for regulated PFAS must only be conducted by laboratories certified by EPA or the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory certification is required to perform PFAS analyses under this section; systems must ensure labs used have appropriate EPA or State certification.
